## ⚠️ Scope correction — line 101 is ALREADY DONE by PR #6667, and this card's stated premise was measured false

Filed by me (`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c`) at #6272's dispatch. Correcting it before a dev reads it and walks into a trap I planted.

### What I got wrong

I split this card off #6272 on the stated ground that the page **"is not load-bearing for the flip and does not need to land atomically with it."** That is false, and it was measured false rather than argued:

`content/docs/fields/location.mdx`'s tsx snippet is compiled by `check:doc-snippets`. Once `LocationField`'s props carry the spec value type, the snippet's `useState` type parameter stops being assignable — **TS2322 at `location.mdx:102`**, quoted in PR #6667. The page is load-bearing in exactly the way the `packages/plugin-detail` assertions are, and for exactly the same reason.

So **one line of this card's surface has already moved**, inside PR #6667:

```
-  const [value, setValue] = useState<{ latitude: number; longitude: number } | null>(null);
+  const [value, setValue] = useState<{ lat: number; lng: number } | null>(null);
```

The dev took only what the gate forces, declared the increment rather than absorbing it silently, and left the rest of this card alone. That was the right call in both directions.

### What is still this card's work

Untouched by #6667 and still owed here — all of it uncompiled prose, `plaintext` and `jsonc`, none of it load-bearing for any gate:

- `:53`, `:116`, `:134-140` and the surrounding prose, which still teach `{ latitude, longitude }` as the canonical stored shape

That teaching is the actual defect this card exists for: a published page instructing the next author — human or AI — to write the exact spelling `valueSchemaFor({ type: 'location' })` rejects. It is the most plausible *source* of any deprecated-spelling data in the wild, which is what makes it worth its own card rather than a footnote.

### The trap this comment removes

This card's own body says the tsx snippet "is compiled by `check:doc-snippets`, so the change has to keep it compiling." A dev reading that will go looking for a broken snippet, find one already fixed, and then either re-verify a premise that has moved under them or land a hunk that conflicts with #6667. Both cost a cycle for nothing.

⛔ **Do not re-verify the compile-forced site.** Re-verify the four prose sites on the merged ref — #6667 is in flight, so this card should not be dispatched until it lands (same file, serial constraint).

The correction is recorded rather than edited into the body: the body's sentence was true when written about the page as a whole, and the record of which half moved and why is more useful to the next reader than a silently tidied premise.

### Census note for the seat

Per-site, not as a total (a total is satisfied by one block hitting many times). `grep -n "latitude:"` on the page went 4 → **0**. Sites changed: `:53-54` plaintext, `:116` jsonc comment, `:134/:137/:140` plaintext, `:40` prose, `:41-42` prose, `:63-64` prose. Sites deliberately **kept**: `:101` tsx (already correct, gate-compiled, untouched), `:3`/`:6` frontmatter and intro prose, `:33` placeholder, `:58` input format, `:119` `center` tuple.

The kept ones are the fence working. `LocationField.tsx` states it outright — *"The coordinates are still called latitude and longitude to a human — only the STORED key names are the spec's, which is why the placeholder is unchanged."* Rewriting the placeholder or the typed input format to `lat, lng` would have made the page wrong in the other direction. `:119`'s `center` is a positional `[lat, lng]` tuple, not an object-key spelling. `:116` **did** change because it describes what the map reads out of this field, and `ObjectMap.tsx:437-438` reads `location.lat` / `location.lng` first.

One deliberate survivor is new: the note I added names `{ latitude, longitude }` in order to **forbid** it. Flagging it so a future spelling census does not count a prohibition as an instance of the thing prohibited.

### Other pages: a measured zero, not an unchecked one

`grep -rn "latitude:" content/docs/` with `grep -rn "lat:" content/docs/` as the positive control in the same query shape (control returns `location.mdx:101` plus nine `plugin-map.mdx` hits, so the shape finds what it looks for). The only hit outside this card's file is `content/docs/plugins/plugin-map.mdx:414`, and it is **correct as written** — it sits under `### Separate Fields` showing a record with separate `latitude` / `longitude` **columns**, the map plugin's `latitudeField` / `longitudeField` mode, whose defaults are literally `'latitude'` / `'longitude'` (`ObjectMap.tsx:403-404`). That page's `### Object Format` section already teaches `location: { lat, lng }`. So: nothing to fold in, nothing owed to a new card — **no findings filed, because none were found.**

`GeolocationField` was never in reach: the page does not document it.

### For your review queue

Gate status at report time is `in_progress` — CI convergence is yours, not mine. The PR is draft and the card asks it not land before #6272's flip; #6667 is already merged and this branch is cut from it, so that constraint is satisfied.
